sample.task:
(Natsuki wakes up and gently holds one of her 3-year-old triplet daughters.)

Natsuki: “Jeez…being a single mother is hard.”

(Just then, there’s a knock on the door. It must’ve been from one of her club members.)

Natsuki: “Come in!”

(Monika enters the room - and she was 5 months pregnant. Her 5-year-old son, Ryū, with her.)

Ryū: (running up to Natsuki for a hug) “Aunt Natsuki!”

Natsuki: (smiling and embracing Ryū) “Hey there, little guy! How are you today?”

Ryū: “I’m good! Mommy says I’m going to be a big brother soon!”

Natsuki: (looking at Monika with a mix of surprise and excitement) “Is that true, Monika? Congratulations!”

Monika: (grinning) “Thank you, Natsuki! Yes, it’s true. Baby number two is on the way.”

Natsuki: “That’s wonderful news! I’m so happy for you.”

(Ryū’s attention is caught by Natsuki’s triplets.)

Ryū: (curious) “Who are they, Aunt Natsuki?”

Natsuki: (gently introducing her daughters) “These are my three beautiful daughters, Hana, Yumi, and Sakura.”

Hana: (shyly) “Hi.”

Yumi: (giggling) “Nice to meet you, Ryū!”

Sakura: (playfully) “Can we play together?”

Ryū: (excitedly) “Yes! Let’s play hide-and-seek!”

Natsuki: (chuckles) “Alright, but be careful, okay? And remember, they are younger than you.”

Monika: “I’ll keep an eye on them too. It’ll be fun!”

(The kids eagerly run off to play while Monika and Natsuki have a chance to catch up.)

Monika: “So, how are you managing as a single mom, Natsuki?”

Natsuki: (sighs) “It’s definitely tough. Balancing work, taking care of the girls, and making sure they’re happy and healthy…it’s a lot. But seeing them grow and thrive makes it all worth it.”

Monika: “I can imagine. Motherhood isn’t easy, but you’re doing an amazing job.”

Natsuki: (grateful) “Thank you, Monika. I appreciate your support. And congratulations again on your growing family. It’s going to be even more chaotic and wonderful for you with two little ones.”

Monika: (laughs) “I’m excited for the chaos. And don’t hesitate to reach out if you ever need any help or even just someone to talk to, okay?”

Natsuki: (smiling) “I won’t hesitate, thanks Monika. We’ve got each other’s backs, right?”

Monika: (nodding) “Absolutely. We’re a club of friends, after all.”

(As Natsuki watches the children playing happily together, she feels a sense of warmth and support, knowing she’s not alone in this journey of motherhood. Just then, Sayori bursts into the room - her 7 month bump is contracting rapidly.)

Hana, Yumi, Sakura, and Ryū: “Aunt Sayori?!”
sample.chosen:
Natsuki: (surprised) "Sayori! Is everything alright?"

Sayori: (panting) "I... I think it's time... The baby is coming!"

Monika: (quickly) "Natsuki, call an ambulance! I'll help Sayori."

Natsuki: (nods and grabs her phone) "Right away!"

(Natsuki calls for an ambulance while Monika helps Sayori sit down comfortably.)

Monika: (calmly) "Breathe, Sayori. Everything will be fine. The ambulance is on its way."

Sayori: (nervously) "I'm scared, Monika... What if something goes wrong?"

Monika: (smiling reassuringly) "Don't worry, Sayori. You're strong, and you can do this. We're all here for you."

(The children gather around, looking concerned.)

Ryū: (worried) "Is Aunt Sayori okay?"

Natsuki: (comforting her daughters) "Aunt Sayori is going to be just fine, sweethearts. She's having her baby, and the doctors will help her."

(The ambulance arrives, and the paramedics quickly assess Sayori's condition.)

Paramedic: (professionally) "We need to get her to the hospital immediately. You can follow us there."

(Monika and Natsuki nod, gathering their children and preparing to head to the hospital.)

Natsuki: (to her daughters) "Let's go, girls. We're going to see Aunt Sayori's baby being born!"

(The group excitedly follows the ambulance to the hospital, ready to support Sayori as she welcomes her new baby into the world.)

(At the hospital, Sayori gives birth to a healthy baby girl, whom she names Aiko.)

Sayori: (tearfully) "Thank you all for being here with me. I couldn't have done it without your support."

Monika: (smiling) "We're always here for you, Sayori. Congratulations on your beautiful baby girl."

Natsuki: (happily) "Welcome to the world, Aiko! You're going to have so many playmates with all of our kids!"

(The friends share a heartwarming moment, grateful for the love and support they have found in each other as they navigate the joys and challenges of motherhood.)
sample.rejected:
Natsuki's eyes widened in alarm as Sayori stumbled into the room, her face pale and her breathing labored. 

"Sayori! What's wrong?" Natsuki rushed to her side, her heart pounding.

Sayori clutched her stomach, her voice strained. "I... I think it's time."

Monika immediately sprang into action. "Ryū, sweetheart, why don't you go play with your cousins for a bit? Mommy needs to help Aunt Sayori."

Ryū, sensing the urgency, nodded solemnly and retreated to the other children, who were now watching with wide, curious eyes.

"Natsuki, call an ambulance!" Monika instructed, her voice calm despite the panic rising within her. "I'll help Sayori get comfortable."

Natsuki fumbled for her phone, her fingers trembling. "Okay, okay, I'm calling!"

As the ambulance sirens wailed in the distance, Natsuki felt a wave of fear wash over her.  She had never experienced childbirth before, and the thought of Sayori going through it alone, with only her and Monika present, was terrifying.

"Sayori, you're going to be okay," Natsuki said, trying to sound reassuring. "The ambulance is on its way. Just breathe."

Sayori squeezed Natsuki's hand, her face pale but determined. "I'm scared, Natsuki."

"I know, Sayori," Natsuki replied, her voice soft. "But you're strong. You can do this."

Monika, ever the calm and collected one, helped Sayori into a comfortable position on the floor. "Just focus on your breathing, Sayori," she said gently. "We're here for you."

The room was filled with a tense silence, broken only by the sound of Sayori's labored breaths and the distant wail of the approaching ambulance. Natsuki held her breath, praying that everything would be alright.
